identity.name: Sodium potassium tartrate
identity.chemical_class: Tartrate salt (mixed sodium and potassium salt of L(+)-tartaric acid)

function.mechanism: Provides buffering and tartrate-ion complexation; in cheese systems acts as an emulsifying salt supporting homogeneous melt and texture while contributing pH control.

adi.basis: Group ADI for L(+)-tartaric acid-tartrates (E334-337, E354), expressed as tartaric acid (EFSA Journal 2020;18(3):6030).

efsa.key_finding: No indication of genotoxicity; no carcinogenicity indication in chronic rat data reviewed; refined exposure estimates did not exceed the group ADI.

adi.basis: ADI range shown as 0-30 mg/kg bw for potassium sodium L(+)-tartrate, expressed as L(+)-tartaric acid (WHO JECFA database).

concerns.summary: Case-series and case reports on high-dose related tartrate exposures (cream of tartar/tartaric acid contexts) describe acute kidney injury in dogs and severe hyperkalemia in humans under non-typical ingestion conditions.
EFSA re-evaluation reported no indication of genotoxic potential for tartaric acid and sodium/potassium tartrates at evaluated uses.
A subchronic rat study on an iron-sodium tartrate complex (not E337 itself) found GI/inflammation-related effects at higher doses; relevance to standard E337 food use is limited.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no carcinogenicity indication in chronic rat data reviewed.
EFSA found no genotoxicity indication for tartaric acid/tartrate salts.
EFSA refined exposure scenario did not exceed ADI across assessed population groups.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2020 reported no ADI exceedance in the refined non-brand-loyal scenario for assessed population groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators retain approval/GRAS status; EFSA established a group ADI with no exceedance in refined exposure assessment; severe effects are mainly linked to atypical high-dose ingestion of related tartrate preparations rather than normal E337 food use.
key_factors: FDA GRAS affirmation in 21 CFR 184.1804 with GMP use conditions
JECFA ADI range 0-30 mg/kg bw with last evaluation year listed as 1973
No IARC listing identified for sodium potassium tartrate
Limited direct modern human epidemiology specific to E337
